title: access channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support (capability id afbws.access.channel.v1). Freemium access model: tier (who) x capabilities (personal permissions) x mode (what is available now), see common.v1.json#/$defs/access. Messages mirror the backend's access database (tables tiers, user_roles, group_roles, users, subscriptions); the model does not know a concrete authorization provider — external groups are addressed by (`provider`, `group_id`). Same convention as afbws.link/afbws.screener: ONE schema id per operation (`afbws.access.<op>.v1`, no .request/.response suffixes); the same schema is the request and its response (echoes `request_id`); response-only fields are forbidden in a request. `request_id` is required in every client request. Two staff tiers are reserved by code: `admin` and `manager` (staff = admin + manager). Staff operations (admin and manager): `users.list`, `user.set` (trial end / manual grant / personal capabilities), `policy.get`/`policy.set` (mode policy of tiers), `stats` (weekly conversion). Admin-only operations: `user.tier.set` (personal tier), `tiers.get`/`tiers.set` (tiers and their limits), `groups.get`/`groups.set` (provider group assignments). Any other connection gets error `forbidden`. Server-initiated: `afbws.access.denied.v1` — the gate's refusal of a request of ANY channel (sent on the refused request's channel, with its `request_id`). Changes of the connection's own effective access arrive as an afbws.auth.v1 push. Whole-request failures of this channel: `afbws.access.error.v1`. See AFB/docs/ws/access.md.

provider.description: Authorization provider (adapter) id: who authenticates the user and supplies its groups, e.g. `getcourse`, `local`. An open set defined by the backend's adapters, not an enum.

window.description: Daily time window, Moscow time: `from` — start, `to` — end. `to` < `from` = across midnight (e.g. 22:00-02:00).

policy.description: Mode policy of a tier (`tiers.policy` in the backend's access database). A tier WITH a policy is `full` (with the limits of `as_tier`) while a manual grant, the trial, a time window (stage 3: a showcase instrument) is active, otherwise `basic` with its own limits. A tier without a policy (null) is always `full` with its own limits. The `trade` capability and a subscription tier are always `full`.

trial_days.description: Trial length in days; 0 or absent = no trial.

workday.description: Window of a trading day (MOEX calendar); null or absent = no window.

weekend.description: Window of a non-trading day (MOEX calendar); null or absent = no window.

tierRow.description: One tier (one row of the `tiers` table without `policy`; the policy is edited by afbws.access.policy.*).

title.description: Label shown in the staff UI.

rank.description: Priority when a user matches several tiers (higher wins); unique among tiers. `admin` = 999 and `manager` = 100 are fixed by code, other tiers 1..99 (checked by the server). The tier with the minimal rank is the default for users not matched by any `user_roles`/`group_roles` row.

subscription.description: Subscription tier: subscription periods are logged on login, the tier counts in conversion; without a policy always `full`. Always false for `admin`/`manager`.

policyRow.description: Mode policy of one tier (afbws.access.policy.*). Staff tiers (`admin`, `manager`) have no policy and are not listed.

policy.description: Mode policy; null — always `full` with its own limits.

tierLabel.description: A tier and its label (for choosing a tier in the staff UI).

capabilityLabel.description: A capability and its label; the set and the labels are defined by the backend code (the frontend does not hardcode them).

groupRole.description: Assignment of a tier or a capability to every member of an external group (one row of the `group_roles` table).

role.description: A tier name (from `tiers`) or a capability name (set defined by the backend code).

group_id.description: Group id at the provider, as a string.

userRow.description: One user who has logged in at least once (row of the `users` table + resolved tier/capabilities + the last subscription period). `provider` — who authenticates the user and supplies its groups. `tier`/`capabilities` — effective (personal `user_roles` ∪ provider groups `group_roles`); `personal_tier`/`personal_capabilities` — the personal `user_roles` assignments only (editable; group assignments are visible in `capabilities` but not edited from here).

personal_tier.description: Personal tier (at most one `user_roles` row with a tier role); null — tier by groups / default.

personal_capabilities.description: Personal capabilities (`user_roles` rows with a capability role).

trial_started_at.description: null — the trial has never been given.

grant_until.description: Manual extension: `full` until this moment; null — none.

subscription.description: The last subscription period; null — never subscribed.

showcase.description: Instrument showcase (stage 3): instruments of the global catalog collection `collection` work as in `full`.

collection.description: Id of a global catalog collection; null — not chosen.

subscription.description: One subscription period (row of the `subscriptions` table).

providerGroup.description: A group of an authorization provider (a hint for choosing `group_roles`).

statsWeek.description: One calendar week of conversion statistics.

usersList.title: afbws.access.users.list.v1 — all users (request / response), staff.
usersList.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response: `items[]` — every user who has logged in at least once (no server-side filtering or paging), `tiers[]` and `capabilities[]` — labels for the staff UI.

tiers.description: Response only: all tiers (incl. staff) with labels.

capabilities.description: Response only: all capabilities with labels.

userSet.title: afbws.access.user.set.v1 — set a user's trial end, manual grant and/or personal capabilities (request / response), staff.
userSet.description: Request: `user_id` + `trial_ends_at`, `grant_until` and/or `capabilities` (at least one; null removes the trial end / grant; `capabilities` replaces the personal capabilities). The first `trial_ends_at` for a user without a trial (`trial_started_at` null) also sets `trial_started_at` = now. Response: `user_id` + `item` — the updated row. Unknown user -> error `not_found`.

trial_ends_at.description: Request only: new trial end; null — remove the trial end.

grant_until.description: Request only: manual grant until; null — remove the grant.

capabilities.description: Request only: the user's personal capabilities, replace-all ([] — remove all personal ones; group capabilities are not affected).

userTierSet.title: afbws.access.user.tier.set.v1 — set a user's personal tier (request / response), admin only.
userTierSet.description: Request: `user_id`, `tier` — the personal tier (any tier incl. `admin`/`manager`) or null (remove: tier by groups / default). Response: `user_id` + `item` — the updated row. Unknown user / tier -> error `not_found` / `validation_error`; removing the last `admin` assignment -> `validation_error`.

tier.description: Request only: personal tier; null — remove the personal tier.

policyGet.title: afbws.access.policy.get.v1 — mode policies of tiers (request / response), staff.
policyGet.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response: `tiers[]` — every non-staff tier with its policy.

policySet.title: afbws.access.policy.set.v1 — set the mode policy of one tier (request / response), staff.
policySet.description: Request (request-only fields): `tier` (not `admin`/`manager`), `policy` (null — no policy: always `full` with own limits). Response: as afbws.access.policy.get.v1. Unknown tier -> `not_found`; staff tier -> `validation_error`.

policy.description: Request only: new policy; null — remove.

tiersGet.title: afbws.access.tiers.get.v1 — tiers and their limits (request / response), admin only.
tiersGet.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response: `tiers[]` — every tier incl. `admin`/`manager` (policies — afbws.access.policy.get.v1).

tiersSet.title: afbws.access.tiers.set.v1 — replace the tiers (request / response), admin only.
tiersSet.description: Request: `tiers[]` — replace-all of the `tiers` table without policies: the policy of a kept tier is preserved, a new tier gets no policy (null). Invariants (checked by the server, `validation_error` with the reason in `message`): `tier` names unique; `admin` and `manager` present with their fixed `rank`/`subscription` (only `title` and `limits` change); other ranks 1..99, unique; a tier cannot be removed while referenced by `user_roles`/`group_roles`/`policy.as_tier` (the message lists the references). Response: the saved tiers, as afbws.access.tiers.get.v1.

tiers.description: Tier names must be unique (JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by key — the server rejects duplicates with validation_error).

groupsGet.title: afbws.access.groups.get.v1 — provider group assignments (request / response), admin only.

provider_groups.description: Response only: groups of the authorization providers (hints for choosing `group_roles`).

provider_groups_error.description: Response only: why provider groups could not be fetched (fully or partly); null — fetched.

groupsSet.title: afbws.access.groups.set.v1 — replace the provider group assignments (request / response), admin only.
groupsSet.description: Request: `group_roles[]` — replace-all of the `group_roles` table (unknown tier/capability or removing the last `admin` assignment -> `validation_error`). Response: as afbws.access.groups.get.v1.

provider_groups.description: Response only: groups of the authorization providers (hints for choosing `group_roles`).

provider_groups_error.description: Response only: why provider groups could not be fetched (fully or partly); null — fetched.

stats.title: afbws.access.stats.v1 — weekly conversion statistics (request / response), staff.
stats.description: Request: `from`, `to` (dates, inclusive, Moscow). Response echoes `from`/`to` and carries `weeks[]` (oldest first), one per calendar week intersecting the range. `new_users` — users whose `first_seen_at` falls in the week; `trials_started` — users whose `trial_started_at` falls in the week; `converted` — subscription periods started in the week; `active` — users whose `last_seen_at` falls in the week.

denied.title: afbws.access.denied.v1 — the access gate refused a request of ANY channel (server -> client).
denied.description: Answer to a request of any schema-first channel that the current `mode` does not allow. `channel` is the channel of the REFUSED request and `request_id` echoes it, so the per-channel request/response client rejects the pending request. `reason`: `basic` — feature not available in basic mode; `showcase` — basic mode with showcase, the instrument is not in the showcase; `held` — activation of an alarm/trade plan while the owner's objects are held. `feature` — gate feature id (e.g. `datasets`, `participants`, `virtual`, `screener`, `alarm.activate`). `message` — ready-to-show text (includes when `full` becomes available, if known).

error.title: afbws.access.error.v1 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).
error.description: `code` is a closed subset of common errorCode: `forbidden` (the operation is not allowed for the connection's tier: not staff / not admin), `validation_error`, `not_found` (unknown user / tier), `invalid_channel`, `invalid_schema`, `internal_error`.
